explanation: Bitwise operators in C, such as AND (&) and right shift (>>), are used to manipulate individual bits in an integer. They are essential for tasks like decomposing a memory address into components (e.g., page number and offset) in systems programming, enabling efficient and low-level data handling without unnecessary overhead.
code_example: unsigned int offset = address & (page_size - 1);  // Extract lower 14 bits
unsigned int vpn = address >> 14;  // Shift right by 14 bits for upper 18 bits
example_explanation: This program takes a 32-bit address and uses bitwise AND (&) to isolate the offset (lower 14 bits) by masking with (page_size - 1), and bitwise right shift (>>) to extract the VPN (upper 18 bits) by shifting the address right by 14 bits, demonstrating how these operators decompose the address as described in the concept.
